gloss: to demonstrate; to display; to exhibit

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {発揮|はっき}しませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {発揮|はっき}していなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {発揮|はっき}していませんでした

definitions.gloss: to demonstrate; to display; to exhibit
definitions.explanation: To bring out and show one's ability, power, or qualities effectively. Used when someone fully utilizes or manifests an inherent quality or capacity.

examples.japanese: {実力|じつりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する。
チームワークを{発揮|はっき}して{試合|しあい}に{勝|か}った。
examples.english: We won the game by demonstrating teamwork.

examples.japanese: {緊張|きんちょう}していたが、{本番|ほんばん}では{持|も}ち{前|まえ}の{集中力|しゅうちゅうりょく}を{発揮|はっき}することができた。
examples.english: I was nervous, but during the actual performance I was able to display my natural concentration.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with を to mark the quality being demonstrated. The subject brings out something they inherently possess — it is not used for acquiring new skills, but for making existing ones visible or effective.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実力|じつりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する (demonstrate one's ability)
- {能力|のうりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する (display one's talent)
- {力|ちから}を{発揮|はっき}する (exert one's strength)
- リーダーシップを{発揮|はっき}する (show leadership)
- {威力|いりょく}を{発揮|はっき}する (demonstrate power/effectiveness)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {示|しめ}す: to show — more general; can show things to others, not limited to inherent qualities
- {見|み}せる: to show/display — focuses on making something visible to others, while {発揮|はっき}する emphasizes bringing out latent ability
